questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity, so its unit is kilogram metre per second.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the SI unit used for linear momentum.

questions.prompt: Which quantity is measured in newton seconds?
questions.explanation: Impulse is force multiplied by time and has the same unit as change in momentum.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate impulse to force acting over time.

questions.prompt: In uniform circular motion, which acceleration always points towards the centre of the circle?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration changes the direction of velocity while pointing towards the centre.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise centripetal acceleration in circular motion.

questions.prompt: What does Archimedes' principle state about a body immersed in a fluid?
options: It experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of fluid displaced
It loses all its mass in the fluid
It experiences no force if it is fully submerged
It displaces fluid equal to its own weight in all cases
questions.correctAnswer: It experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of fluid displaced
questions.explanation: The buoyant force on an immersed body equals the weight of the displaced fluid.
questions.learningOutcome: State Archimedes' principle for bodies in fluids.

questions.prompt: Which factor directly increases pressure at a point in a liquid of uniform density?
options: Larger surface area of the container
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure increases with depth because a deeper point supports more liquid above it.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify factors affecting pressure in liquids.

questions.prompt: Which gas law relates pressure and volume when temperature is constant?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law states that pressure is inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: Name the gas law for pressure-volume changes at constant temperature.

questions.prompt: What does specific heat capacity describe?
options: Energy needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1 kelvin
Energy needed to melt any mass at its melting point
Force needed to stretch a spring by 1 metre
Pressure needed to reduce a gas volume by half
questions.correctAnswer: Energy needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1 kelvin
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity compares how much energy different substances need for the same temperature rise.
questions.learningOutcome: Define specific heat capacity in terms of energy, mass, and temperature change.

questions.prompt: Which wave is longitudinal when it travels through air?
questions.explanation: Sound in air travels through compressions and rarefactions parallel to the direction of travel.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sound in air as a longitudinal wave.

questions.prompt: Which law relates the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction?
questions.explanation: Snell's law describes refraction when a wave passes between media of different optical density.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall the law used to analyse refraction at a boundary.

questions.prompt: What is the focal length of a converging lens?
options: Distance from the optical centre to the principal focus
Distance from the object to the lens
Width of the lens at its centre
Angle between incident and emergent rays
questions.correctAnswer: Distance from the optical centre to the principal focus
questions.explanation: The focal length gives the distance from the lens centre to the point where parallel rays meet.
questions.learningOutcome: Define focal length for a converging lens.

questions.prompt: Which relationship represents Ohm's law for a metallic conductor at constant temperature?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that potential difference is proportional to current when resistance is constant.
questions.learningOutcome: State Ohm's law using voltage, current, and resistance.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux measures the total magnetic field passing through an area and is measured in webers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the SI unit used for magnetic flux.

questions.prompt: What does Lenz's law describe?
options: The direction of induced current opposes the change causing it
The heating effect of current in a resistor
The bending of light at a boundary
The inverse relation between gas pressure and volume
questions.correctAnswer: The direction of induced current opposes the change causing it
questions.explanation: Lenz's law gives the direction of induced current in electromagnetic induction.
questions.learningOutcome: State Lenz's law for induced currents.

questions.prompt: What is the photoelectric effect?
options: Emission of electrons from a surface when light of sufficient frequency falls on it
Splitting of a white beam into colours by a prism
Production of heat when current passes through a resistor
questions.correctAnswer: Emission of electrons from a surface when light of sufficient frequency falls on it
questions.explanation: Photoelectrons are released when incident photons have enough energy to overcome the work function.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the photoelectric effect in terms of electron emission.

questions.prompt: What is meant by the half-life of a radioactive sample?
options: Time taken for half of the unstable nuclei to decay
Time taken for all radiation to stop instantly
Time taken for mass to double
Time taken for temperature to halve
questions.correctAnswer: Time taken for half of the unstable nuclei to decay
questions.explanation: Half-life measures how quickly a radioactive sample decays by halves.
questions.learningOutcome: Define half-life for radioactive decay.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg trolley moves at 3 m/s. What is its momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum equals mass times velocity, so p = 2 x 3 = 6 kg m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate momentum from mass and velocity.

questions.prompt: A 20 N force acts on a football for 0.5 s. What impulse is given to the ball?
questions.explanation: Impulse equals force multiplied by time, so impulse = 20 x 0.5 = 10 N s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate impulse from force and contact time.

questions.prompt: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: Multiplying velocity by time gives displacement, so the graph area gives displacement.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret the area under a velocity-time graph.

questions.prompt: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a horizontal circle. In which direction is the centripetal force?
options: Towards the centre of the circle
Away from the centre of the circle
questions.correctAnswer: Towards the centre of the circle
questions.explanation: The inward force keeps changing the direction of the stone's velocity.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the direction of centripetal force in circular motion.

questions.prompt: A learner pushes a crate with a constant force of 50 N through 4 m. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work done equals force times distance moved in the direction of the force.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate work done by a constant force.

questions.prompt: Why can a hydraulic press multiply force?
options: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally
Liquids have no mass in a closed system
Large pistons always move faster than small pistons
Air pressure disappears inside the press
questions.correctAnswer: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle allows a small force on a small area to produce a larger force on a larger area.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain force multiplication in hydraulic machines.

questions.prompt: Which formula gives the pressure due to a liquid of density rho at depth h?
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure depends on density, gravitational field strength, and depth.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the relationship between liquid pressure, density, gravity, and depth.

questions.prompt: Why are many dam walls built thicker at the bottom?
options: Water pressure is greater at greater depth
Water is colder near the top
Atmospheric pressure is zero at the bottom
Concrete expands only near the base
questions.correctAnswer: Water pressure is greater at greater depth
questions.explanation: The bottom of a dam must withstand larger liquid pressure than the top.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply pressure-depth ideas to structures such as dams.

questions.prompt: An object floats in water because its average density is lower than water. What happens to the object?
options: It displaces enough water for upthrust to balance its weight
It sinks until it touches the bottom
Its volume becomes equal to zero
questions.correctAnswer: It displaces enough water for upthrust to balance its weight
questions.explanation: A floating body settles until the upward buoyant force equals its weight.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate floatation to density and upthrust.

questions.prompt: In steady flow of an incompressible fluid, what happens to speed when a pipe becomes narrower?
questions.explanation: The continuity equation requires the same volume flow rate through wider and narrower sections.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply continuity ideas to fluid speed in pipes.

questions.prompt: At constant pressure, a gas volume increases when its kelvin temperature increases. Which law is shown?
questions.explanation: Charles' law states that gas volume is directly proportional to kelvin temperature at constant pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the pressure-constant relationship between gas volume and temperature.

questions.prompt: What is 27 degrees Celsius expressed approximately in kelvin?
questions.explanation: Kelvin temperature is approximately Celsius temperature plus 273.
questions.learningOutcome: Convert Celsius temperature to kelvin for thermal calculations.

questions.prompt: How much heat raises 2 kg of water by 10 kelvin if its specific heat capacity is 4200 J/kg K?
questions.explanation: Using Q = mc delta T gives Q = 2 x 4200 x 10 = 84000 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate heat energy using mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change.

questions.prompt: Why does temperature remain constant while pure ice is melting at its melting point?
options: Energy is used to overcome bonds during change of state
The mass of ice becomes zero instantly
questions.correctAnswer: Energy is used to overcome bonds during change of state
questions.explanation: Latent heat changes state without raising temperature during the phase change.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain constant temperature during melting using latent heat.

questions.prompt: In a sufuria of water heated from below, why does warmer water rise?
options: It becomes less dense than the cooler water around it
It loses all its heat instantly
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes less dense than the cooler water around it
questions.explanation: Convection occurs because heated fluid expands, becomes less dense, and rises.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain convection in liquids using density changes.

questions.prompt: A sound wave has speed 340 m/s and wavelength 0.85 m. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Using v = f lambda, f = 340/0.85 = 400 Hz.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate frequency using wave speed and wavelength.

questions.prompt: A wave has a period of 0.02 s. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is the reciprocal of period, so f = 1/0.02 = 50 Hz.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the relationship between frequency and period.

questions.prompt: Which conditions are needed for total internal reflection?
options: Light moves from denser to less dense medium and incidence angle exceeds critical angle
Light moves from air to glass at any angle
Light strikes a rough opaque wall
Light travels only through a vacuum
questions.correctAnswer: Light moves from denser to less dense medium and incidence angle exceeds critical angle
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs only beyond the critical angle when light tries to leave a denser medium.
questions.learningOutcome: State the conditions for total internal reflection.

questions.prompt: Which description fits the image formed by a plane mirror?
options: Virtual, upright, and same size as the object
questions.correctAnswer: Virtual, upright, and same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a laterally inverted virtual image the same size as the object.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the image properties of a plane mirror.

questions.prompt: A device uses 12 V and draws 2 A. What power does it consume?
questions.explanation: Electrical power is P = VI, so P = 12 x 2 = 24 W.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate electrical power from voltage and current.

questions.prompt: Three resistors of 2 ohm, 3 ohm, and 5 ohm are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistances in series add directly: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 ohm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate equivalent resistance for series resistors.

questions.prompt: Two 6 ohm resistors are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: Two equal resistors in parallel have half the value of one resistor.
questions.learningOutcome: Find equivalent resistance for equal parallel resistors.

questions.prompt: How does an electric fuse protect a circuit?
options: It melts and breaks the circuit when current is too large
questions.correctAnswer: It melts and breaks the circuit when current is too large
questions.explanation: A fuse wire heats up and melts when excessive current could damage appliances or wiring.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the protective action of a fuse.

questions.prompt: What is the shape of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor?
options: Straight lines parallel to the conductor only
Radial lines pointing away from the conductor
No field unless the conductor is coiled
questions.explanation: The right-hand grip rule shows circular magnetic field lines around a straight current.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the magnetic field pattern around a straight conductor.

questions.prompt: A transformer has 1000 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. If the primary voltage is 240 V, what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, so Vs = 240 x 250/1000 = 60 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the transformer turns ratio to calculate secondary voltage.

questions.prompt: An object is projected horizontally from a table. Which statement about its motion is accurate if air resistance is ignored?
options: Horizontal velocity is constant while vertical velocity increases downward
Both horizontal and vertical velocities remain constant
Vertical motion stops until the object reaches the floor
questions.correctAnswer: Horizontal velocity is constant while vertical velocity increases downward
questions.explanation: Projectile motion combines constant horizontal velocity with accelerated vertical motion due to gravity.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse horizontal and vertical components of projectile motion.

questions.prompt: A 4 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s2. What resultant force acts on it?
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives F = ma = 4 x 3 = 12 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate resultant force using mass and acceleration.

questions.prompt: A block needs a friction force of 15 N to move steadily across a horizontal surface. If the normal reaction is 50 N, what is the coefficient of friction?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of friction is friction divided by normal reaction: 15/50 = 0.30.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine coefficient of friction from frictional force and normal reaction.

questions.prompt: What is the kinetic energy of a 0.5 kg ball moving at 20 m/s?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is 1/2 mv2, so 1/2 x 0.5 x 20 x 20 = 100 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate kinetic energy from mass and speed.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg trolley moving at 3 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg trolley and they stick together. What is their common speed after collision?
questions.explanation: Total momentum before collision is 6 kg m/s, shared by a combined mass of 3 kg.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply conservation of momentum to a simple inelastic collision.

questions.prompt: A body moves in a circle of radius 2 m at a speed of 4 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is v2/r, so 4 x 4 divided by 2 gives 8 m/s2.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate centripetal acceleration from speed and radius.

questions.prompt: A machine has useful output work of 150 J when 200 J is supplied. What is its efficiency?
questions.explanation: Efficiency is useful output divided by input, multiplied by 100 percent.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate efficiency from energy input and useful output.

questions.prompt: A spring extends by 0.04 m when a force of 20 N is applied. What is its spring constant?
questions.explanation: From Hooke's law, k = F/x = 20/0.04 = 500 N/m.
questions.learningOutcome: Use Hooke's law to determine spring constant.

questions.prompt: Taking g as 10 N/kg, what pressure is exerted by water of density 1000 kg/m3 at a depth of 0.5 m?
questions.explanation: Using p = rho g h gives p = 1000 x 10 x 0.5 = 5000 Pa.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate hydrostatic pressure using density, gravity, and depth.

questions.prompt: A hydraulic jack has a small piston area of 0.01 m2 and a large piston area of 0.20 m2. What load force is produced by a 50 N effort?
questions.explanation: Equal pressure gives F2 = F1 x A2/A1 = 50 x 0.20/0.01 = 1000 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate output force in a hydraulic system using piston areas.

questions.prompt: A stone weighs 8 N in air and 5 N when fully immersed in water. What is the upthrust on the stone?
questions.explanation: Upthrust equals the loss of apparent weight, so 8 N minus 5 N gives 3 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate upthrust from apparent weight loss in a fluid.

questions.prompt: Why does an object appear lighter when weighed while immersed in water?
options: Water exerts an upward upthrust on the object
The object's mass disappears in water
The weighing scale measures volume only
questions.correctAnswer: Water exerts an upward upthrust on the object
questions.explanation: The apparent weight is reduced by the upward buoyant force from the displaced water.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain apparent weight loss of bodies in fluids.

questions.prompt: Strong wind blowing over a loose iron-sheet roof can lift the sheet. Which idea explains this effect?
options: Faster air above the roof has lower pressure
Faster air above the roof has greater density
The roof loses all its weight
Air below the roof becomes a vacuum always
questions.correctAnswer: Faster air above the roof has lower pressure
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle links higher fluid speed with lower pressure along a streamline.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Bernoulli's principle to pressure differences in moving air.

questions.prompt: At constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is doubled. What happens to its volume?
options: It becomes four times as large
questions.explanation: Boyle's law gives an inverse relationship between pressure and volume.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Boyle's law to pressure and volume changes.

questions.prompt: How much energy is needed to melt 0.2 kg of ice if the specific latent heat of fusion is 334000 J/kg?
questions.explanation: Using Q = mL gives Q = 0.2 x 334000 = 66800 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate latent heat energy from mass and specific latent heat.

questions.prompt: A hot metal block is placed in cooler water inside an insulated container. Which equation expresses heat balance if no heat is lost?
options: Heat lost by metal = heat gained by water
Heat gained by metal = heat lost by water
Temperature lost by metal = mass gained by water
Specific heat of metal = volume of water
questions.correctAnswer: Heat lost by metal = heat gained by water
questions.explanation: In an insulated system, energy lost by the hotter body is gained by the cooler body.
questions.learningOutcome: Set up heat balance for bodies at different temperatures.

questions.prompt: Under which conditions does a real gas behave most like an ideal gas?
questions.explanation: Molecules are far apart and intermolecular forces are less significant at low pressure and high temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify conditions under which ideal gas assumptions are most valid.

questions.prompt: A learner hears an echo 0.6 s after clapping near a cliff. If sound speed is 340 m/s, how far away is the cliff?
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back, so distance = vt/2 = 340 x 0.6/2 = 102 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate distance using echo time and speed of sound.

questions.prompt: Light travels at 3.0 x 10^8 m/s in vacuum and 2.0 x 10^8 m/s in glass. What is the refractive index of the glass?
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = speed in vacuum divided by speed in medium, so n = 3.0/2.0 = 1.5.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate refractive index from wave speeds.

questions.prompt: For glass of refractive index 1.5 in air, which critical angle is closest to the actual value?
questions.explanation: For a glass-air boundary, sin C = 1/n = 1/1.5, giving C close to 42 degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: Estimate critical angle using refractive index.

questions.prompt: Using lens magnitudes, a converging lens has focal length 10 cm and object distance 30 cm. What is the image distance?
questions.learningOutcome: Use the thin lens formula to find image distance.

questions.prompt: An object is 30 cm from a lens and its image is 15 cm from the lens. What is the magnification magnitude?
questions.explanation: Magnification magnitude is image distance divided by object distance, so 15/30 = 0.5.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate lens magnification from image and object distances.

questions.prompt: A current of 2 A flows for 5 minutes. How much charge passes a point in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Charge Q = It, and 5 minutes is 300 s, so Q = 2 x 300 = 600 C.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate charge flow from current and time.

questions.prompt: A 60 W lamp operates for 120 s. How much electrical energy does it use?
questions.explanation: Energy used equals power multiplied by time: E = 60 x 120 = 7200 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate electrical energy from power and time.

questions.prompt: A uniform wire keeps the same material and cross-sectional area, but its length is doubled. What happens to its resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length when material and area stay the same.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how wire length affects electrical resistance.

questions.prompt: Two equal resistors are connected in series across a 12 V supply. What voltage is across each resistor?
questions.explanation: Equal series resistors share the supply voltage equally.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine voltage division across equal series resistors.

questions.prompt: Why is the terminal potential difference of a cell lower than its emf when current flows?
options: Some energy per coulomb is lost across internal resistance
The emf becomes zero in every closed circuit
Current stops flowing through the external circuit
questions.correctAnswer: Some energy per coulomb is lost across internal resistance
questions.explanation: A current through internal resistance causes a lost voltage inside the cell.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the difference between emf and terminal potential difference under load.

questions.prompt: Which rule is commonly used to find the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
questions.explanation: The left-hand rule gives the motor effect direction for force, field, and current.
questions.learningOutcome: Select the rule for force direction on a current in a magnetic field.

questions.prompt: How can the induced emf in a simple generator be increased?
options: Rotate the coil faster in the magnetic field
Use a coil with no turns
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate the coil faster in the magnetic field
questions.explanation: A faster change of magnetic flux produces a larger induced emf.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify factors that increase induced emf in a generator.

questions.prompt: An ideal transformer has 100 V and 2 A on the primary side. If the secondary voltage is 20 V, what is the secondary current?
questions.explanation: In an ideal transformer, input power equals output power, so 100 x 2 = 20 x Is.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conservation of power in an ideal transformer.

questions.prompt: A falling object reaches terminal velocity in air. Which force relationship is then true?
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the resultant force is zero, so drag balances weight.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse terminal velocity in terms of balanced forces.

questions.prompt: Why are some road bends banked for vehicles moving at speed?
options: A component of the normal reaction helps provide centripetal force
Banking removes the need for gravity
Banking makes friction act vertically upward only
The vehicle's mass decreases on the bend
questions.correctAnswer: A component of the normal reaction helps provide centripetal force
questions.explanation: On a banked road, the support force has an inward component that helps turn the vehicle.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain centripetal force on a vehicle moving around a banked bend.

questions.prompt: Why do crumple zones in vehicles reduce injury during a collision?
options: They increase stopping time, reducing average force for the same momentum change
They increase the passenger's momentum before impact
They make the collision last zero seconds
They remove the need for seat belts
questions.correctAnswer: They increase stopping time, reducing average force for the same momentum change
questions.explanation: For a given impulse, a longer stopping time lowers the average force on occupants.
questions.learningOutcome: Use impulse concepts to explain collision safety features.

questions.prompt: For a projectile launched and landing at the same level with fixed speed, which angle gives maximum range if air resistance is ignored?
questions.explanation: The range is greatest when horizontal and vertical components are balanced at 45 degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how launch angle affects projectile range.

questions.prompt: A cart rolls down a smooth track from rest. Which energy change mainly explains its increasing speed?
options: Gravitational potential energy changes into kinetic energy
Chemical energy changes into nuclear energy
Sound energy changes into gravitational potential energy
Kinetic energy changes only into elastic energy
questions.correctAnswer: Gravitational potential energy changes into kinetic energy
questions.explanation: As height decreases on a smooth track, gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse energy transformations in mechanical systems.

questions.prompt: Why does engine oil usually flow more easily after an engine warms up?
options: Its viscosity decreases as temperature rises
Its pressure is independent of temperature
questions.correctAnswer: Its viscosity decreases as temperature rises
questions.explanation: Many liquids become less viscous when warmed, so they flow more readily.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate temperature changes to viscosity and flow of liquids.

questions.prompt: A small steel ball falling through oil eventually moves at constant speed. Why does this happen?
options: Viscous drag plus upthrust balance its weight
The ball's mass becomes equal to zero
Gravity stops acting below the oil surface
The oil exerts no forces on moving objects
questions.correctAnswer: Viscous drag plus upthrust balance its weight
questions.explanation: Terminal speed in a viscous fluid occurs when upward forces balance the ball's weight.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain terminal speed of a body moving through a viscous fluid.

questions.prompt: Water rises in a narrow glass capillary tube mainly because of which effect?
options: Adhesion between water and glass exceeds cohesion within water
Atmospheric pressure is zero inside the tube
Gravity pulls water upward in the tube
questions.correctAnswer: Adhesion between water and glass exceeds cohesion within water
questions.explanation: Capillary rise occurs when adhesive forces pull the liquid up along the tube walls.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain capillary action using adhesive and cohesive forces.

questions.prompt: A horizontal pipe narrows and water flows steadily through it. What happens in the narrower section according to Bernoulli and continuity ideas?
options: Both speed and pressure become zero
Density doubles and speed remains unchanged
questions.explanation: Continuity gives higher speed in the narrower section, and Bernoulli's principle links that to lower pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine continuity and Bernoulli ideas for flow through a constriction.

questions.prompt: Why can a real heat engine not convert all absorbed heat into useful work in a cycle?
options: Some heat must be rejected to a cooler sink
Energy is not conserved in engines
Work can only be produced at absolute zero
The engine must have no moving parts
questions.correctAnswer: Some heat must be rejected to a cooler sink
questions.explanation: The second law of thermodynamics prevents a cyclic engine from being 100 percent efficient.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why practical heat engines have efficiency below 100 percent.

questions.prompt: Why does a blackened absorber plate improve a solar water heater?
options: Black surfaces absorb more radiant energy
Black surfaces reflect all infrared radiation
Black surfaces lower the Sun's temperature
questions.correctAnswer: Black surfaces absorb more radiant energy
questions.explanation: Dull black surfaces are good absorbers of thermal radiation.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply radiation properties to solar heating devices.

questions.prompt: A fixed mass of gas is kept at constant volume. If its kelvin temperature doubles, what happens to its pressure?
questions.explanation: At constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to kelvin temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse pressure changes for a gas at constant volume.

questions.prompt: In a stationary wave on a string, what is the distance between two neighbouring nodes?
questions.explanation: Adjacent nodes in a stationary wave are separated by lambda/2.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate node spacing to wavelength in stationary waves.

questions.prompt: A siren on a moving ambulance approaches a stationary listener. What happens to the observed pitch?
options: It is higher than when the ambulance is stationary
It is lower than when the ambulance is stationary
It is independent of relative motion
questions.correctAnswer: It is higher than when the ambulance is stationary
questions.explanation: Approach compresses wavefronts, increasing observed frequency and pitch.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain pitch changes due to relative motion of source and observer.

questions.prompt: When is diffraction through a gap most noticeable?
options: When the gap size is comparable to the wavelength
When the gap is infinitely larger than the wavelength
Only when waves travel in a vacuum
Only when the wave has zero frequency
questions.correctAnswer: When the gap size is comparable to the wavelength
questions.explanation: Diffraction is strongest when wavefronts pass through openings similar in size to their wavelength.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse factors affecting diffraction of waves.

questions.prompt: Why must the cladding of an optical fibre have a lower refractive index than the core?
options: To allow total internal reflection inside the core
To absorb all light before it reaches the end
To make the fibre conduct electric current
To prevent any change in light direction
questions.correctAnswer: To allow total internal reflection inside the core
questions.explanation: A lower-index cladding lets light in the core reflect internally at suitable angles.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of core and cladding refractive indices in optical fibres.

questions.prompt: An object is placed between F and 2F in front of a converging lens. Which image is formed?
options: Virtual, upright, diminished, and between lens and F
Real, upright, same size, and at F
questions.explanation: A converging lens forms a magnified real image beyond 2F for an object between F and 2F.
questions.learningOutcome: Predict image properties for object positions in front of a converging lens.

questions.prompt: What physical principle is behind Kirchhoff's current law at a circuit junction?
questions.explanation: The total current entering a junction equals the total current leaving because charge is conserved.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret Kirchhoff's current law using conservation of charge.

questions.prompt: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, what is true about the current through the galvanometer?
options: It is twice the branch current
questions.explanation: At balance, the two junctions connected by the galvanometer are at the same potential.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the balance condition of a Wheatstone bridge.

questions.prompt: Why does Lenz's law agree with conservation of energy?
options: The induced current opposes the change, so external work is needed to maintain the change
The induced current always increases the change without limit
It makes electrical resistance equal to zero
It removes magnetic fields from all circuits
questions.correctAnswer: The induced current opposes the change, so external work is needed to maintain the change
questions.explanation: If induced currents helped the change causing them, energy could appear without work being done.
questions.learningOutcome: Connect Lenz's law with energy conservation.

questions.prompt: A pendulum experiment is used to determine g. Which graph gives a straight line whose gradient can be used to find g?
questions.explanation: For a simple pendulum, T2 = 4 pi2 L/g, so the gradient of T2 against L is 4 pi2/g.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a graphical method for estimating gravitational field strength using a pendulum.

questions.prompt: A designer wants a suspension system with lower effective spring constant using identical springs. Which arrangement best achieves this?
options: Use only one spring and shorten it
Heat the springs until they glow
questions.explanation: Springs in series extend more for the same force, giving a lower effective spring constant.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate spring arrangements for a required effective stiffness.

questions.prompt: Water flows steadily from a wide pipe into a narrower horizontal pipe. Which design concern is most important if pressure in the narrow section becomes too low?
options: Cavitation or air bubble formation may damage the pipe or pump
The water temperature must become absolute zero
The pipe must stop obeying continuity
The water density must become infinite
questions.correctAnswer: Cavitation or air bubble formation may damage the pipe or pump
questions.explanation: Very low pressure in fast-moving liquid can allow vapour bubbles to form and collapse destructively.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate a practical risk caused by pressure changes in fast fluid flow.

questions.prompt: Which set of features would make a simple solar water heater most effective?
options: Black absorber, transparent cover, and insulated back
Shiny white absorber, open top, and metal back exposed to air
Clear absorber, black outlet pipe only, and no insulation
Thick glass absorber, silvered water, and no sunlight
questions.correctAnswer: Black absorber, transparent cover, and insulated back
questions.explanation: Good design increases radiation absorption while reducing heat losses by convection, radiation, and conduction.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate thermal design features for efficient solar heating.

questions.prompt: Why should engineers avoid forcing a bridge or machine part at its natural frequency?
options: Resonance can produce large oscillations and possible failure
questions.correctAnswer: Resonance can produce large oscillations and possible failure
questions.explanation: At resonance, energy transfer to the system is efficient and amplitude can grow dangerously.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate resonance risks in physical structures and machines.

questions.prompt: A capacitor of capacitance C is charged to voltage V. Which expression gives the energy stored?
questions.explanation: The energy stored in a capacitor is proportional to capacitance and to the square of voltage.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the energy relationship for a charged capacitor.

questions.prompt: What output is produced by a bridge rectifier connected to an AC supply before smoothing?
options: Pure steady DC with no ripple
questions.explanation: A bridge rectifier makes current pass through the load in the same direction during both half cycles.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the output of a bridge rectifier circuit.

questions.prompt: In a transistor switch circuit, what does a small base current usually control?
options: The gravitational field around the circuit
The colour of the battery casing
The mass of the load resistor
questions.explanation: A transistor can use a small input current to switch or amplify a larger output current.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the control role of base current in a transistor switch.

questions.prompt: In a photoelectric experiment above threshold frequency, what mainly increases when light intensity is increased but frequency is kept constant?
options: Number of emitted electrons per second
Maximum kinetic energy of each electron
questions.correctAnswer: Number of emitted electrons per second
questions.explanation: Higher intensity supplies more photons per second, increasing emission rate when photon energy is already sufficient.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how intensity and frequency affect photoelectric emission.

questions.prompt: Which idea explains why nuclear fission releases a large amount of energy?
options: A small loss of mass is converted into energy according to E = mc2
Atoms lose all their protons without any energy change
Chemical bonds store all nuclear energy
Energy is created without any mass-energy relationship
questions.correctAnswer: A small loss of mass is converted into energy according to E = mc2
questions.explanation: In nuclear reactions, mass defect is converted into energy following Einstein's mass-energy relation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain nuclear energy release using mass-energy equivalence.
